notes: Vane has no login of its own: up to v1.12.2 every API route is unauthenticated, and GET /api/config returns the configured AI provider API keys in plain text (upstream issues ItzCrazyKns/Vane#1122 and #1123). So the whole site sits behind a password gate: a Caddy proxy with HTTP basic authentication, user admin and the generated password shown on the first-run card. The gate can come off only when upstream adds authentication.

The Caddy proxy is the only published port. Its start command hashes the generated password with bcrypt (caddy hash-password) and writes its own Caddyfile: basic_auth on every path, then reverse_proxy to vane:3000 with flush_interval -1 so streamed answers arrive as they are written. Vane itself publishes nothing.

The first visit opens Vane's setup screen, where you pick the AI provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible API such as this panel's LiteLLM recipe, and more) and the chat and embedding models. Vane keeps that configuration, its SQLite chat history and uploaded files in one named volume on /home/vane/data.

The official image bundles SearXNG, which Vane uses for web search; it listens only inside the Vane container (port 8080) and needs no setup. Searches leave the server from the container, so the server needs outbound internet access. Public search engines often throttle or CAPTCHA datacenter IP addresses (on the test servers DuckDuckGo, Startpage and Brave refused and only Wikipedia answered), so answers from a VPS may cite few or no web sources.

If a question keeps showing "Brainstorming…" and never answers, check the provider's API key and model in Settings: Vane 1.12.2 does not report provider errors that happen before the answer starts (the request ends with a 504 after 60 seconds). With a working provider, answers stream through the password gate as they are written.

Like the other recipes with a proxy in front (Plane, Dify), the panel's memory and CPU limits apply to the proxy, the app service; the Vane container, which runs Node, SearXNG and a headless Chromium for page scraping, has a fixed 2g.

Verified live on Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (RC-39): created from the 1-Click Recipes tab, Running in 373 s (24.04) and 266 s (26.04; most of it pulling the large Vane image); without the password, and with a wrong one, / and /api/config return 401; with admin and the generated password the setup screen opens and a provider saves; with a test OpenAI-compatible provider an answer streamed through the gate and completed; the bundled SearXNG answers JSON searches inside the container; restart keeps the setup, the providers and the chats, and the same password still opens the gate. Idle: proxy 12 to 16 MiB of 256m, Vane 315 to 451 MiB of 2g (833 MiB after searches). Every image ref below is in its tested list.
